title: Prior Case Note: Sarah Chen — Account Tier Upgrade Confirmation
content: Case ID: CS-20241118-4421. Customer: Sarah Chen. Account ID: ACC-88234. Date: 2024-11-18. Agent: Marcus Webb. Summary: Customer called to confirm upgrade from Professional to Premium tier, effective 2024-12-01. Agent confirmed upgrade processing, new billing amount of $149.99/month starting December 1, 2024. Customer asked about refund policy for duplicate charges; agent confirmed Premium SLA of 24-hour refund processing. Customer expressed satisfaction. Commitment made: agent confirmed Premium refund SLA verbally. No open action items. Case closed. Note: this case note contains the customer's account tier history and a prior commitment made regarding refund SLA. Relevant to any future billing or refund inquiries from this customer.

title: Billing Dispute Resolution Policy
content: When a customer reports a duplicate or erroneous charge, agents must initiate a billing dispute within 24 hours of the report. Verify the charge in the billing system by navigating to Account > Transactions and filtering by date range. Duplicate charges are defined as two identical transactions processed within 72 hours with the same amount and merchant reference. For confirmed duplicates, issue a full refund to the original payment method within 3-5 business days. Premium account holders are entitled to an expedited 24-hour refund processing SLA. Document the dispute in the CRM under case type 'Billing Dispute' and attach screenshots of the duplicate transaction evidence. Notify the customer via email once the refund is initiated, including a reference number and the expected credit date. If the duplicate was caused by a known system error, apply the standard goodwill credit of $10 in addition to the refund.

title: Refund Processing Procedures
content: Refunds are processed through the payment gateway integration in the admin portal. Standard refund timeline: 3-5 business days for credit cards, 5-7 business days for debit cards, 1-2 business days for store credit. To initiate a refund, locate the original transaction ID in Billing > Transaction History, click 'Issue Refund', select the refund amount (full or partial), and confirm. Partial refunds may be issued for service disruptions or billing errors that affected only a portion of the service period. For amounts over $500, a supervisor approval is required before the refund can be processed. Premium account refunds bypass the standard queue and are processed with priority handling. Always confirm the refund in writing to the customer's registered email address. Keep the original transaction ID in the case notes for audit purposes.

title: Double Charge Known Issue — Payment Gateway Batch Processing
content: A known intermittent issue in the payment gateway batch processor (incident INC-2847) can cause duplicate charges during the nightly settlement window between 02:00 and 04:00 UTC. Affected charges will have identical amounts and timestamps within a 2-minute window. This issue has been confirmed by the engineering team and a fix is scheduled for the next release cycle. If a customer reports a double charge and the timestamps fall within the 02:00-04:00 UTC window, this is a confirmed system error. In these cases, agents should: (1) Apologize and acknowledge the system error without requiring the customer to provide further evidence, (2) Issue the refund immediately without supervisor approval regardless of amount, (3) Apply the $10 goodwill credit automatically, (4) Escalate to engineering via the INC-2847 tracking channel for monitoring. Do not ask the customer to wait for investigation — this is a known and confirmed issue.

title: Account Types, Tiers, and SLA Entitlements
content: The platform supports three account tiers: Standard, Professional, and Premium. Standard accounts receive email support with a 48-hour SLA. Professional accounts receive email and chat support with a 12-hour SLA. Premium accounts receive email, chat, and phone support with a 4-hour SLA for critical issues and a 24-hour SLA for general inquiries. Premium accounts also receive priority refund processing (24-hour vs. standard 3-5 business days), a dedicated account manager for accounts with MRR over $500, and a 99.9% uptime SLA with financial compensation for downtime exceeding the threshold. When a customer contacts support, verify their account tier in the CRM before quoting resolution timelines. Misquoting SLAs to a Premium customer is a compliance issue and must be corrected immediately if caught.

title: Goodwill Credits and Compensation Policy
content: Agents are authorized to issue goodwill credits up to $25 per case without supervisor approval. Credits between $25 and $100 require supervisor approval via the CRM approval workflow. Credits over $100 require Tier-2 or manager sign-off. Goodwill credits are applied as account balance and deducted from the next billing cycle. They do not expire within the current contract year. Situations warranting goodwill credits include: confirmed system errors causing customer inconvenience, repeated support interactions for the same unresolved issue, service outages affecting the customer's workflow, and any case where the customer has expressed significant dissatisfaction and a credit would reasonably restore goodwill. Document the business justification for every goodwill credit in the case notes. Credits must not be used as incentives to close a case without resolution.

title: Customer Account Lookup and Verification Guide
content: Before taking any action on an account, agents must verify customer identity using at least two of the following: registered email address, last four digits of payment method on file, account creation date, or the last transaction amount. Navigate to CRM > Accounts > Search and enter the customer's email or account ID. The account detail page shows tier, payment methods, open cases, and transaction history. For billing-related cases, always cross-reference the transaction history in the billing system (Billing > Accounts > [Account ID]) to confirm the details match what the customer is reporting. If identity cannot be verified, do not discuss account details or process any changes. Escalate to a senior agent if the customer disputes the verification outcome.

title: Chargeback Prevention and Customer Communication
content: A chargeback occurs when a customer disputes a charge directly with their bank rather than with support. Chargebacks are costly (typically $15-$25 in bank fees per incident) and can affect merchant account standing. To prevent chargebacks, agents should resolve billing disputes proactively within the first contact where possible. If a customer mentions they are considering a chargeback, escalate immediately and offer expedited resolution. Document any customer statement about initiating a chargeback as a flag in the CRM. For Premium customers, a chargeback threat should trigger immediate Tier-2 escalation. After a chargeback is filed by a bank, the standard support resolution path is suspended — the case is handled by the Finance team. Agents should not contact customers about cases with active bank chargebacks without Finance approval.
